slides.headline:
Korea's coffee city began
with beach vending machines.
slides.subline: Terarosa Coffee Factory, 7 Hyeoncheon-gil, Gujeong-myeon, Gangneung — roasting since 2002, listed as open year-round by Korea's national tourism office, and sitting inland rather than on the coffee street it gets credited for

slides.label: The year Terarosa opened in Gangneung — not as a cafe, but as a roasting factory supplying beans to other people's cafes and hotels. The counter came later, because visitors kept turning up wanting to drink what was being roasted
slides.note: Sources: Korea Tourism Organization English listing — address, phone, hours, open year-round · The Korea Economic Daily (KED Global) — 2002 roasting factory, factory-cafe concept, cafe density figures · Korean business press, 7 April 2026 — founder's full exit, 34 stores, revenue · Checked 13 September 2026

items.d: Anmok Beach was a quiet strip of raw-fish restaurants. Taxi drivers ferrying sightseers out there fed coins into roadside coffee machines, and visitors copied them. Korean press records local radio stations running debates over which machine's coffee tasted best. Travel coverage puts the first two proper cafes on that strip at 1998

Kim Yong-deok left roughly two decades in banking, returned to his hometown of Gangneung and installed a roasting plant inside a shop — a format Korean business press credits as the country's first factory-style cafe. That is Terarosa, and it is not on the beach

Park Yi-chu, born 1950 in Kyushu to a Zainichi Korean family, had run Gabae Bohemian in Seoul's Hyehwa-dong since 1988. Encyclopedic sources date his move to Gangneung to 2004, via Pyeongchang in 2000; some travel write-ups instead put him at Anmok from 2000. In 2022 the ministry for SMEs listed his shop as a long-established business

slides.title:
The famous one isn't
on the famous street.
slides.body:
Search "Gangneung coffee" and you get two things: a half-kilometre of seafront cafes at Anmok, and the name Terarosa. Most people assume they are one trip. Terarosa's original sits inland at Gujeong-myeon; Anmok is on the coast.

The nickname is earned, though. The Korea Economic Daily reports about 25 cafes per 10,000 residents here against 14 nationally, and roughly 1,200 cafes along the Gangwon coast with some 45 percent in Gangneung alone.

What makes Terarosa worth the detour is the direction of it. It did not start by selling coffee to tourists. It sold beans to the people who sold coffee to tourists, and the cafe was a by-product of that.

As of 2026 the founder has gone. Korean business press reported on 7 April 2026 that Kim sold his entire 24.2 percent stake to a private equity firm in July 2025 — a full exit after 23 years, from a chain now at 34 branches. Whether that changes what is in the cup is not something we can tell you from a desk.

items.d: Phone +82-33-648-2760. Korea's national tourism office lists it as open year-round with no regular closing day. This is the 2002 original, and it is inland — check the address before setting off for the sea
Per the same listing, last orders 20:30 and 16:00. Hours on tourism listings drift, so confirm on the day rather than on arrival

items.t: It is a compound, not a counter
items.d: The tourism listing describes a roastery with a cafe, bakery, restaurant, art shop and museum on one site. Pour-over is the listed speciality. No official prices are published there, so we are not quoting any

items.t: Anmok Coffee Street is the other half of the trip
items.d: About 40 cafes along half a kilometre of seafront, plus a few surviving vending machines kept as a nod to how it started. Korea's first municipal coffee festival has run here since 2009. KTX from Seoul puts the city under two hours away

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal visit.
Every fact here is from a published source, checked on 13 September 2026.
slides.by:
Sources disagree on when Park Yi-chu actually reached Gangneung — 2000 or 2004 — so we have shown both rather than picking one.
Ownership changed in 2025 and hours can drift; whether the coffee is worth a two-hour train is a personal question, and yours.

caption:
Gangneung is called Korea's coffee city. It started with beach vending machines, not baristas.

Terarosa opened inland in 2002 as a roasting factory, not a cafe — and it isn't on the coffee street.

Ownership changed in 2025; taste is personal.

Sources in the last slide. Save it.
